subject: Mental Models
title: Hanlon's Razor
description: Learn Hanlon's Razor in one minute.

hook.text: A colleague does not reply to your email for three days. You assume they are ignoring you.

buildup.text: Hanlon's Razor says never attribute to malice what can be explained by incompetence, forgetfulness.

discovery.text: Robert Hanlon popularized this maxim in 1980, though similar ideas date back to Goethe and Napoleon.

twist.text: Assuming malice triggers defensive behavior. Defensive behavior looks aggressive to others.

climax.text: Give people the benefit of the doubt. Most failures are caused by confusion, not conspiracy.

punchline.text: Assume confusion before malice. You will be right more often.
